Where the repo carries no docs/agents/ overlay at all (e.g. a skill-source repo), substitute the closest repo doctrine you can find (README, CONTRIBUTING, top-level docs) and record the substitution — do not treat those paths as guaranteed to exist. Before you open any source file, resolve and read the map input: run py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/map_orient.py orient --root /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills/.worktrees/567-k-one-spine-mutable-middle --work-id 567-k. On RESOLVED, read the entrypoint it names and the packets, overlays and decision anchors it routes you to for the area the ask touches, and treat every later source read as confirming a frame the map already gave you rather than building one out of code. On DEGRADED, re-run the same command with --substitute PATH (what you read instead of a map — it is hash-pinned into the receipt) --unmapped TEXT (what stayed unmapped) --escalation TEXT (what you are escalating, and to whom), and get that on the record before any source read: degraded is a declared reading, never a licence to start from code. The tool probes a fixed fallback order — README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, a docs/ index — and labels a substitute it found there as verified by the filesystem rather than merely asserted by you. The anchor of this instruction is the point: 'before you open any source file' is an act you cannot postpone, whereas a map-first imperative anchored to a late artifact (the gate plan, which is authored at the END of a long run) is satisfied by a run that crawls source for fifty calls, reads the map afterwards, and has complied exactly — that is measured behaviour, not a hypothetical. plan.title: Author the gate plan
plan.imperative: Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the map input the context step resolved, using templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md (intent; affected capabilities; relevant examples/events; structural anchors; governing constraints/assumptions; decision anchors and decision pressure; claims/evidence surfaces; map confidence/staleness/disputes; out of scope). Write it to .agent-work/567-k/MISSION_FRAME.md — that exact path is what the c6 gate reads, so a frame parked anywhere else reads as no frame at all. For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; c6 is waivable, so take that escape as a RECORDED waiver (<engine> waive plan --cond c6 --authority human --reason '...') rather than as a silent skip. The c6 gate runs map_orient.py verify-frame over that file: every anchor id the frame cites must exist in the map inventory the context step resolved, or — when context came back DEGRADED — must be one of the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned there, so the frame is compared against a committed prior declaration instead of a same-breath assertion. Know what that check is and is not, and do not overclaim it: it is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return, not the fix for map-LATENESS. Measured against this epic's baseline five runs it has sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and it inherits the late-anchor defect it was built next to, because anchors-in-a-late-frame is compliance without sequence. The load-bearing map-first anchor is at the context step ('before you open any source file'), which is why verify-orientation is gated there and verify-frame is gated only here. Do NOT 'fix' that asymmetry by also running verify-frame at context: no frame exists at context — the step runs before understand and plan — and the only way to make it pass there is to let an ABSENT frame pass, which is exactly the refusal the whole check is built on. If verify-frame ever has to be context-safe, give it a step-scoped mode; never a vacuous pass. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone. Then author the gate plan into execute.json: each gate the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. Get the human to approve it. In delegated mode, satisfy c3 (plan approved) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's frozen plan and scope -- by default via the spine_evidence MCP tool (action=attach, task_id=plan, evidence_type=user-decision, fields={cite: 'LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'}); CLI fallback: attach plan --type user-decision --field cite='LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'; surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral rather than blocking on the human. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

execute.context_headroom_note: #467. Absolute-token context reserve for THIS gate only: the engine subtracts it from both the soft and hard caps before dividing by the model's window, so `execute` may not be BEGUN with less than this much room left below the hard cap. It makes the imperative's existing prose instruction ('ensure context headroom before entering') enforceable, and it can only ever tighten -- no gate can raise a threshold. WHY 30000, and it is a GUESS, revisable in place: `execute` is the run's longest gate and the one that cannot be abandoned halfway, because it drives every crew gate and each crew dispatch costs tens of thousands of tokens. The only observation available was a commander sitting at ~127K fill after a cold resume plus one full three-task gate -- which bounds one gate's marginal cost in the tens of thousands but cannot separate it from the resume baseline. 30K is a round number at the low end of that range: on claude-opus-5 (1M window, 80K soft / 150K hard) it moves execute's begin-work line from 15% to 12% and its advisory from 8% to 5%, while every other gate keeps the shipped default. The named settle experiment (read fill_fraction across completed commander runs at the moment execute was started) is NOT runnable from existing artifacts -- gauge.json keeps only the latest reading and the per-gate context manifests record no fill -- so a later run may revise this number here, in this one place, without re-deriving anything.

feedback.title: Record workflow feedback
feedback.imperative: Before committing, reflect honestly on how this run actually went: how closely you followed the skills, handoffs, and checklists; where you had to improvise or work around the instructions; what was ambiguous, missing, or contradictory; and what would have helped. Include the crew Workflow Feedback harvested at each gN-integrate. A 'none' answer requires a run-specific reason ('none — confirmed after review: <what you checked>'); a bare 'none' does not close this step. Then record what happened as EPISODES: one episode per distinct thing that happened — not one per run, and not a summary — each stating its task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost and workaround. An episode is a record, not a rule: write what you observed, and do NOT write a rule for a future agent to follow — a rule to follow belongs in docs/agents/* and is a human's call. Write the delta to .agent-work/567-k/episode-delta.json and apply it deterministically: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/567-k/episode-delta.json --store-root episodes. Pass --store-root on every invocation: the writer's default resolves relative to the installed skill directory, so an installed copy would silently build a store at ~/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/episodes — outside the repo — while every gate reported green. Never hand-edit a file under episodes/: that writer is the only write path into it. Then run the capture gate before advancing: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py 567-k --store-root episodes --phase feedback.

postconditions.statement: this run captured at least one episode: an episode in the store records this work id

archive.title: Archive, commit, and push
archive.imperative: Commit all remaining work, including this run's episodes under episodes/. That is a tracked repo-root path, so the committed episode IS the durable record: it survives `git worktree remove` and lands in a fresh clone. None of the old is-.agent-work-gitignored reasoning applies to it. Push the branch to remote. When you open a PR on Windows, write the body to a temp file and use gh pr create -F <file> — a bash heredoc and a PowerShell @'...'@ here-string both fail for gh pr create --body (here-strings work for git commit -m, not PR bodies). Move .agent-work/567-k/ to .agent-work/archive/<date>-567-k/. Run the archive-phase capture gate before marking archive complete — it additionally requires git to TRACK the episode, which is what proves the record outlived this worktree: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py 567-k --store-root episodes --phase archive. Confirm the branch is clean and merge-ready per repo guidance. The engine mechanically refuses closeout (c4) when the staged diff includes suspicious artifacts (oversized files, generated record dumps, disallowed dirs, binary/blob additions, large data files); if any are intentional, a human waives c4 via <engine> waive archive --cond c4 --authority human --reason "..." rather than hand-editing the spine. Release the engine session lease only as your VERY LAST action, AFTER the archive postconditions pass and you have run the engine's final advance on archive (the advance that marks the spine done): by default call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=release (this is your own spine; the door needs no session id argument). CLI fallback: <engine> release --session-id commander-567-k. Release must come after that closing advance, never before it — the lease must cover every journaled action, so the release is the final journal entry; releasing earlier leaves archive's own closeout entries (attest/waive/advance) after the lease release and fails the terminal provenance check.

postconditions.statement: work area archived and this run's episode captured AND tracked by git, so the record survives this worktree
branch committed and pushed

the work is REACHABLE: this branch has a pull request that is OPEN or MERGED. A merged PR is reachable work; a closed-unmerged one is not, and neither is no PR at all. A terminal spine and a pushed branch describe the run, not the ref -- CI never runs on an unopened branch, and every commander that reached a terminal spine without opening one had to be chased for it. Open the PR even if the work is unfinished; declare FINAL or PENDING in its title and hand the merge up. Two properties of the check text are load-bearing. The branch is derived at CHECK time from the repo root, never resolved at instantiation: init instantiates the spine before it starts the branch, so the branch need not exist yet -- and a literal branch placeholder is not a resolver-owned token, so instantiation cannot catch one and would ship it unsubstituted. The count is compared in the SHELL because the engine's verdict for a command condition is the EXIT CODE and stdout is discarded: gh --jq 'length > 0' prints true or false but exits 0 either way, so that form can never fail.

check.command: test "$(gh pr list --head "$(git -C /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills/.worktrees/567-k-one-spine-mutable-middle rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" --state all --json state --jq '[.[] | select(.state == "OPEN" or .state == "MERGED")] | length')" -gt 0

why_trail.why: Project doctrine loaded and the map read is on record as an explicitly degraded reading, not a silent skip. Two facts change how I plan. First: this repo has no architecture map to plan from — no docs/architecture/ packets, an empty map/ids.jsonl, and a map/INDEX.md whose per-module links do not resolve — so my structural frame for scripts/checklist_engine.py and scripts/mcp_spine_server.py must be built from source and tests, declared as such, rather than presented as map-derived. map/INDEX.md is fenced to the Admiral so I do not repair it. Second: ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT's dogfooding delta is directly load-bearing for #634 — I am editing the engine my own session is running, so every behavioural claim about the engine or door must come from a fresh process with explicit paths, and the launch order's self-hosting pre-ruling (read-only on the live spine, mutating verbs only against a copy) is the same rule stated sharper. The engine also reports the context gauge is SILENT because this session is bound to two candidate spines, so I get no automatic context readings this run and must watch headroom by judgement.

Reconciling the order against the code before planning moved the gap twice, and both moves shrink it. First: amend() at checklist_engine.py:2971 already gives a GATED plan a mutable middle — add/drop/rescope on pending gates, retext-check on a pending or in-progress one, all-or-nothing, with reason+authority landing in cl["amendments"] — and spine_amend already exposes it at the door. So "make the middle mutable" is built. Second: the freeze that exists, _floor() at :3036, is "1 + index of the last non-pending gate", which freezes only what has already been STARTED. That gives the opening bookend for free and gives the closing bookend nothing: reconcile/triage/review/feedback/archive sit pending for the whole run, so at 9b38b9d9 a Commander standing at execute can amend away its own archive, and an Admiral can drop closeout. There is no declared-bookend concept anywhere in the engine or in the three spine templates. That asymmetry is the one genuine engine-level gap #634 names. The second-file middle (execute.json, ADMIRAL_LOG.md + transitions/) is doctrine, not an engine refusal — amend would have accepted both, and verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py does not reference execute.json — so migrating it is a doctrine change whose convergence the order reserves to the human. My first named unknown is answered at source: --from_child (:2617-2645, tests :429-471) reads a child SURVEY's consolidation and attaches it as review-result evidence before the postcondition check; consolidate() is survey-only (:2734), and on BLOCK the advance is refused while the evidence is still attached (:456), so a parent cannot launder a rejection. It is a cross-agent verdict seam that carries evidence UP and never drives a child's gates — not a gated-can't-grow workaround. It survives untouched, and it constrains the design: "one spine per agent" means one agent DRIVES one spine, not that no spine may reference another.

The plan survived a cold critic that found two blocking defects in it, and fixing them changed the run's scope. First defect: g3-proof — the gate that is supposed to BE the empirical proof — closed on two check:null postconditions, which is unfalsifiable by construction and exactly the failure mode this repo names first. Both are now command checks, and I proved they discriminate: each exits 1 against today's tree and can only pass once the guard ships. Second defect: I claimed specs/ in scope while no gate touched it, and the crew half was unbuildable as planned. skills/implementer/templates/IMPLEMENTER_PLAN.template.json is not a *SPINE* template so it was never in my grant — my error, predating the critic — and it is COMPILED from specs/implementer.spine.toml by scripts/generate_spine.py, whose _compile_gate (:669-684) returns a fixed field list with no bookend key. A hand-added declaration would survive until the next regeneration and then vanish, which is an incident this repo has already had and pinned a test against (tests/test_generate_spine.py:1694-1700, "the artifact diverged from its source"). generate_spine.py is in neither my ownership nor lane J's fence, so the crew half is FLOATED to the Admiral rather than hand-patched, and decision:every-planning-role lands for Admiral, Commander and Explorer but not crew. The critic also dissolved the trilemma I had built the comparison around: backward-compatible describes the mechanism's default reading of an undeclared plan, not whether you also run the retrofit against live spines in the same release, so B's compatibility and A's immediate protection are compatible after all — and a fourth option (positional opening, declared closing) exists that no candidate saw. That is now in the comparison, credited, and flagged as not yet self-attacked. My recommendation stays B with the ship-time retrofit attached, and the convergence stays the human's.

All eight gates of execute.json are closed and its lease released; the commander REPLAN_INPUT verifier exits 0. Delivered: amend() freezes a declared bookend against drop, rescope, retext-check and against an add landing past it, read through one swappable helper so the human can still change the declaration form by changing one function; and the three role spine templates this lane owns declare their bookends, pinned by a test asserting the exact flagged-id set rather than "something is flagged". Both crew gates carried an independent APPROVE, and g1's reviewer proved the new tests go red before green rather than reporting that they do. Self-hosting holds under the engine I patched: read-only on both live spines exits 0, the exact three-drop delta that succeeded at 9b38b9d9 is refused on a copy, the middle still grows, and a mixed delta rolls back so the legal op does not land either. Full suite 3383 passed, 0 FAILED at eb94b150 in a clean detached worktree, with only the Admiral-owned MapTreeFreshness deselection, which I verified genuinely fails rather than assuming it. Two things are NOT delivered and are floated rather than hidden: the crew half of decision:every-planning-role, because IMPLEMENTER_PLAN is compiled by generate_spine.py whose _compile_gate drops unknown keys and which neither lane owns; and the "capture the plan changed" half, still served only by amend's pre-existing amendments trail. The convergence between design candidates is deliberately not taken — it is the human's.

Reconciled directly rather than through a Cartographer, because there is no packet map in this repo and that verdict was already on record from the context step rather than discovered convenient here. The structural record that actually exists is docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md, which declares itself the tracker of shipped engine behaviour, so the bookend key, rescope's widened overwritable list, and a new Bookends subsection went there. Reconciling turned up one thing I did not expect and did not fix: the projection does not render the flag, so an agent reading current cannot see which gates are frozen — and reading spine.json to find out is itself a violation under global-everyone. The schema doc's own Rendering section had already written down why this would happen, in the residual limit it names for TaskFieldCompleteness: a field carried by a template but built by neither the amend-task builder nor append() is invisible to that property. So the suite passing at eb94b150 is not evidence the field is rendered; it is evidence the check cannot see it. Staged as a triage candidate, deliberately deferred until the human picks the declaration form, since rendering a name the human may replace would bake in the wrong one.

Three candidates, all recommend-and-defer, none filed — and the citation records the deferral itself rather than a filing approval, because none was sought and none was authorized. decision:no-issue-filing-mid-run is settled/human with the reason stated: "we've been ballooning out tracking." The discipline worth naming is that I checked the fix-now ladder honestly instead of using the no-filing ruling as cover for skipping the check: each candidate fails a DIFFERENT rung, and candidate 1 is the one I would otherwise have been tempted to fix, since rendering the flag is a small edit. It fails "verifiable now" for an interesting reason — the property test that should have caught the omission is structurally blind to a template-only field, which the schema doc had already written down as its own residual limit. So I could have made the change and had no way to show it was right. It also fails on timing: the human has not yet chosen the declaration form, so rendering a name they may replace would bake in the wrong one. Two items are deliberately NOT in triage: the crew half of every-planning-role and the execute.json migration are scope floats needing an Admiral ownership ruling, and turning a float into a future issue would quietly convert a question I owe upward into a backlog entry nobody answers.

Run summary written to the exact path the order names and committed on the branch, with PR #635 open and verified against the forge rather than inferred. The summary is honest about what it is: delivered for Admiral, Commander and Explorer; NOT delivered for crew, with the reason at source rather than an apology; and deliberately unconverged on the design choice, which is the human's. I put my own mistakes in it — the mis-scoped gate plan, the proof gate whose postconditions could not fail, the question I silently closed, the off-by-one in my own handoff, and the verification command I got wrong — because the previous wave's most useful returns were the ones that indicted their own author, and because three of those five were caught by a critic or a crew rather than by me, which is itself the finding.
